answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should make identity costly where it counts, not everywhere. Picture an annual summit where every agent must post a small bond in copper tokens before its vote counts; cheap fake identities then bleed value instead of flooding consensus. Reputation flows like an ocean current, weighted by bonded stake and peer attestation history, so one operator spinning up a thousand shells gains nothing — each shell needs its own bond and independent attestations, making attacks economically irrational.
